outcomes.title: An operator signs in and reaches the control plane
criteria: The dashboard accepts an access token and shows the primary navigation and the Work view

outcomes.title: An operator creates work and finds it where they look
criteria: A created work item is listed in the work list
A created work item appears in the board's backlog group

outcomes.title: An operator reads an item's criteria and gates
criteria: An item's page shows its criteria, proofs and gates by id and by key

outcomes.title: An operator sees what is tested and whether it passes
criteria: The Tests page lists every case with its recent runs

outcomes.title: Onboarding gives our repository the fast delivery path with nothing extra to wire up
criteria: After normal project onboarding, the project's status shows the fast path on by default: local preview enabled, candidates capped at five changes with a short configurable wait, promotion only for a passing candidate
The path works with GitHub as an optional mirror: no GitHub Actions workflow and no Railway environment is required for the local preview and candidate path
No permanent staging branch and no second test framework appear — the project's own required end-to-end cases are the test

outcomes.title: A change to our Compose application is tested in a preview before it lands
criteria: Before the change's merge was recorded, its declared application cases ran against a preview of exactly that change
The landed change's record names the preview's result and each application case's verdict, and the merge commit that carried it
I can read this from the delivery API without logging into anything else

outcomes.title: Previews keep to themselves and clean up after the run
criteria: Each preview runs with its own application state and database, separate from every other preview, from UAT and from production
Preview resources are bounded and the preview is removed automatically when its run ends
A preview never receives production secrets
The record of a previewed change shows the isolation and the cleanup, so I can trust it rather than take it on faith

outcomes.title: Our static site keeps its preview without Compose
criteria: A static-site change is previewed through the existing static preview path, with no Compose and no Railway required
Its preview verdict is recorded like any other change's
The existing static preview rules still hold unchanged — nothing about the current path was weakened to make this pass

outcomes.title: Up to five passing changes ship together as one exact candidate
criteria: A candidate names the exact changes it was assembled from — at most five — each with its exact source identity
The candidate ran the combined required end-to-end cases of all its changes and every one passed before it could promote
With fewer than five changes ready, the candidate still proceeds after the short configurable wait

outcomes.title: A failed candidate never reaches production and its failure stays on the record
criteria: The candidate that failed a required case shows as failed and was never promoted
Its record names the failing required case and its verdict
The failure remains visible later — in the candidate record and in the Tests history — not erased by the next candidate

outcomes.title: Production serves exactly the release we promoted, and we can see it was verified
criteria: The live production environment is observed serving the exact release identity the passing candidate promoted
The verification is on record — the observation names the served sha and that it was verified — not assumed
The expected release for production is the one the candidate promoted

outcomes.title: The docs explain the fast path to users and operators
criteria: User and operator docs cover the defaults, how a project declares its applications and cases, how previews are isolated, what happens after a failure, and how production is verified
The docs are reachable from the control plane itself, without asking the team or leaving for another tool
